summary: Midnight metadata sweep created a narrow GPU-availability window; long-lived customer streams amplified allocation delays
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-13 00:45 and 01:30 UTC we saw a narrow window (~45m) of reduced GPU availability in the us-west dedicated pool serving VectorAI. Impact: VectorAI reported escalated p95 token latencies, increased allocation retries, and several 5xx errors resulting in degraded throughput for their critical inference routes. Environment: prod cluster us-west, dedicated pool 'vecai-reserved-3'. Observed during our nightly metadata/snapshot audit sweep that scans NVMe and validates checkpoints across nodes. The audit sweep coincided with a surge of long-lived websocket streams from the customer that hold prefetched slots for extended periods, causing slot fragmentation and ephemeral reservation gaps. Autoscaler did not add capacity during the initial window because its attach-failure sampling aggregated below the scale-up threshold (heartbeat compression + sampling windowing).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated pool 'vecai-reserved-3' run the nightly metadata/snapshot audit sweep with concurrent long-lived stream workload (many persistent keepalive connections). 2) Observe allocator slot utilization and NVMe IO during sweep. 3) Send sustained 1000 qps of short inference requests from a synthetic tenant that reuses streams but keeps them alive for >10 minutes. 4) Monitor autoscaler decisions and allocation retries (attach/release churn).
expected_behavior: Metadata/sweep should complete without causing a transient allocation shortage; autoscaler should detect attach failures/pending queues and trigger scale-up within configured cooldown; long-lived streams should not block ephemeral slot reallocation to short burst traffic beyond configured reservation timeout.
actual_behavior: During the sweep: NVMe IO increased and snapshotter briefly held exclusive handles causing allocation handoffs to delay. Long-lived streams retained small prefetched batches and keepalive handles; together they created many micro-fragments in GPU slot accounting. Autoscaler sampling window suppressed scale-up because heartbeat compression and aggregated attach-fail metric stayed under threshold. Result: p95 token latency rose from baseline ~320ms to ~6.8s for affected routes, per-tenant throughput fell by ~45%, and allocation retries spiked (attach Retry count +350% over baseline).

investigation_notes: Timeline: 00:45 audit sweep started; 00:48 first attach retries seen; 00:50 autoscaler sampled below threshold; 01:10 autoscaler triggered manual refresh after ops runbook; 01:30 pool recovered. Hypotheses checked: 1) Snapshotter-exclusive-locks increased NVMe latency and delayed allocation handoffs -> confirmed by nvme iops spike and long snapshotter duration. 2) Long-lived streams from VectorAI prevented slot reclamation beyond normal TTL -> confirmed by elevated keepalive count and prefetched-batches per-connection metric. 3) Autoscaler sampling suppression due to heartbeat-compression and sample-window sizing prevented timely scale-up -> supported by autoscaler logs showing attach-fail-rate=0.08 vs threshold 0.12. Additional evidence: Node-level metrics show increased context-switch and io-wait; allocator traces show fragmentation accounting prevented contiguous slot allocation for 100-token batches. We reviewed related runbook (confluence page) and found sweep runs occasionally configured with higher concurrency on our maintenance schedule. Linked issues: SUP-742998 (snapshotter-induced throughput drop) and SUP-61234 (autoscaler sampling window tuning).
comments: 2026-03-13 02:05 Support - Aisha Khan: Customer reported p95 spike and 5xxs during midnight window. Collected logs and escalated to SRE. Notified customer we're investigating. (ref: slack #support-vectorai)

2026-03-13 03:12 SRE - Mateo Ruiz: Observed NVMe iops spike matching snapshotter run. Found prolonged snapshotter cycle, likely holding exclusive file descriptors. Opening infra PR to limit parallel snapshot concurrency. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123

2026-03-13 04:00 SRE - Priya Patel: Autoscaler sampling window appears to smooth attach-fail signals during short thin windows. Suggest lowering sample-window to 30s for dedicated pools during maintenance windows or enable 'maintenance-aware' scaler bypass.

2026-03-13 05:20 Support - Aisha Khan: Customer confirms long-lived websocket streams are common for their product. Requested recommended configuration changes. Provided temporary mitigation steps (below).

2026-03-14 09:10 Customer - VectorAI (T. Morgan): Appreciate the quick look. We'll trial reducing keepalive timeouts and closing idle streams. Also open to guidance on route pinning & model-variant fallbacks.
ongoing_mitigation: 1) Ops temporarily paused non-critical parts of the metadata sweep at 01:05 UTC to allow pool recovery. 2) Enabled emergency autoscaler override for vecai-reserved-3 at 01:10 to add 2 extra nodes (manual scale-up). 3) Provided VectorAI with a recommended client change: reduce keepalive to 60s and close idle streams after 45s. 4) Short-term infra patch: limit snapshotter concurrency to 2 jobs per-host (PR submitted).
resolution: TBD - under investigation. Next steps: merge infra PR to limit snapshot concurrency, adjust autoscaler sampling/maintenance flaging for scheduled sweeps, and coordinate with VectorAI to reduce long-lived stream TTLs. After changes, we'll run a controlled simulated sweep + synthetic load test during maintenance window to validate. Postmortem and permanent mitigations targeted within 7 days.
communication_plan: Notify VectorAI engineering lead with timeline for each mitigation. Post incident update to #incidents and draft postmortem once root cause confirmed. Follow-up ticket to adjust autoscaler logic and snapshotter runbook.
